free_text_notes.physician_note: 82-year-old woman with hypertension, prior TIA, admitted 5/21 with right pontine lacunar infarct. MRI confirmed small infarct; no hemorrhagic conversion.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Ambulated in hallway with sister present. 5/24 15:00: Amlodipine changed from 5 mg daily to 10 mg daily this morning. Reviewed with patient and sister at 15:00; teach-back correct. A standard nutritional screening was performed on admission. The patient scored within the normal range and no specialist dietitian input was required. A routine ECG was performed on day 3. The result showed no changes compared to the admission ECG. No clinical action is needed.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: Discharge planning in progress; CM following daily. 5/25 07:45: Spoke with sister: no longer able to provide care after discharge because of a new work schedule. Patient cannot manage ADLs alone. Therapy referral still needs to be sent. Bedroom is upstairs at home; setup not reviewed yet. PT recommends assistance with all transfers for now.
